about: What may differ between BN5's battle (the reference) and BN6's with a family moved in (the subject), and why: tools/xdiff.py reads each game's numbers as BN6's (maps), each game's structures through their own layouts (layouts), and replays BN6's draws from BN5's by the twins of its rng, the engine's own draws one game alone makes named there too (rng), and lets a difference pass only where a mask names it (masks), each an engine difference that is not the family's code, with the evidence: both games' routines by address. No mask applies to the family's own records (its objects, what they own, its attacks and effects): what the engine writes there in its own numbers is read as BN6's in the snapshot, as an enemy id is (maps: alliance, renderer, slot), and any other difference there fails the spec (docs/multirom/families.md; docs/devtools/differential.md). No game code here: addresses and numbers only.

name_id.why: An object's NameID (+0x28) is its enemy id: BN5's CanGard family is 0x4F-0x54, moved as BN6's ids 0x200-0x205, and its Handi family 0x13-0x18 as 0x206-0x20B, the families' (src/emu/xvirus_families.c, .first_id; xvirus_recipe.h, XV_FIRST_ID); BN5's Navis by their recipes (src/emu/xnavi_bn5.c, .first_id; src/emu/xnavi_recipe.h, XN_ID_OF): ToadMan's V1-SP 0x143-0x146 as 0x1D8-0x1DB, KnightMan's 0x13D-0x140 as 0x1D4-0x1D7, ShadowMan's 0x12B-0x12E as 0x1C8-0x1CB, NumberMan's 0x131-0x134 as 0x1CC-0x1CF, TomahawkMan's 0x137-0x13A as 0x1D0-0x1D3, Colonel's 0x125-0x128 as 0x1C4-0x1C7, the Dark Soul's 0x18D as 0x1DC, the Darkloids ShadeMan's 0x149-0x14C as 0x1E0-0x1E3 and BlizzardMan's 0x14F-0x152 as 0x1E4-0x1E7; MegaMan is 0x180 in BN5 and 0x1A0 in BN6 (his battle object's NameID in both traces from their first frame).

megaman_forms.why: MegaMan's NameID in a form of BN6's is 0x1AB + the form (0x08015B22 writes it as he crosses: 0x1AC-0x1C3; 0x1A0 in none), where BN5's stays 0x180 through a Soul and its end (the research's runs/nid). His role is MegaMan's whatever his form; his NameID is compared as BN6 writes it for the form BN5's maps to (a Soul behind the proxy, 0x1B3).

chip_id.why: A chip id: BN5's by the chip registry's rows (src/core/xchips_registry.c: a chip both games name alike BN6's id, BN5's other chips the ids of their own), read from the source the game is built from, as BN6's engine has them in its tables (docs/multirom/chip-registry.md). Translated where an object keeps one: a battle object's chip (+0x2A, BN6_T1_CHIP, the chip it uses next, u16, 0xFFFF none: written as the hand deals it to MegaMan and as a virus picks its own) (a virus's held chip picked, or its own code's: Zomon's AreaGrab), and the AI data's places below (its AttackVars +0x14, the chip used, written by the chip's use, BN5 0x0800FF68 / BN6 0x08012824, and by a virus's chip writer, BN5 0x0800FE7C / BN6 0x080126F6: strh r0,[r7,#0x14], r7 the AI data + 0xA0). A virus's CurAction from 0x10 that is the family the chip writer returned for its chip (the record's +0x0B, BN5 0x0800FEBA / BN6 0x0801273A, for setAttack0) is read as BN6's family of BN6's chip (tools/xdiff_snap.py, chip_action): the same chip in each game's own numbers. And where a support chip's routine keeps it: its object's +0x30 (r7 as the support family calls the routine: the chip used, its AttackVars +6 above it; BN5 0x080EC416 / BN6 0x080ED0F8), by the object's type (t4: the fourth kind's). The support chips' objects keep it so: each spawned by its support routine with r7 the chip (and AttackVars +6 above it), stored at +0x30 (MetaGel's 0x21, Blinder's 0x23, Jealousy's 0x36, NrthWind's 0x39, BoyBomb's 0x67, RainyDay's 0x75, BlakWing's 0x54, HolyDrem's 0x59, HotBody's 0x57, the Anti chips' setter 0x2A and its counter 0x2B (spawned by BN5 0x080E38E2 as its trap springs), DarkCirc's 0x5E and DrkSonic's 0x4A (chip_darkcirc, chip_drksonic: 0xBB and 0xC6 there in BN5's, BN6's ids 0xD6 and 0xDC), RockCube's 0x37 (BN5's chip 99, BN6's 143: BN5 0x080E47CE / BN6 0x080E59F6, twins) and Poltrgst's 0x72 (BN5 0x080E8DC2, moved: chip_poltrgst, 213 in BN5's, the registry's 292 in BN6's): their routines BN5 0x080E2F84, 0x080E3228, 0x080E4628, 0x080E493C, 0x080E816E, 0x080E91EE, 0x080E6AB4, 0x080E6F60 HotBody's family 0x080F0222 and the Anti chips' 0x080E380A (0x080E3828), each str r7,[r0,#0x30]); and the third kind's: the Anti chips' trap 0x4D, its setter's chip passed on (BN5 0x080CF7F4: str r7,[r0,#0x30]). A virus's support chip (its held chip's family 0x15 by the chip writer, Zomon's AreaGrab) runs BN5's support family's timing in BN6's engine as family 0x65 (src/emu/xvirus_dispatch.c's XV_SUPPORT: BN6's 0x15 run twice in one frame, the attack ending in its routine's frame as BN5's 0x080EC448 ends it; the families' calls to BN5's chip writer, 0x0800FE6A, aimed at XV_CHIP_WRITER, which gives 0x65 for 0x15): its CurAction BN5's 0x15 read as 0x65 (virus_support), MegaMan's and a Navi's own 0x15 BN6's (tools/xdiff_snap.py, chip_action).
evidence: DarkInvs's object (BN5's fourth kind's 0x18, spawned by its support routine 0x080E2420: str r7,[r0,#0x30], the chip used) keeps its chip at +0x30 as the support objects of BN6's do (chip_darkinvs: BN5's 189, BN6's 289)

chip_id.subs_why: Where an object keeps its chip's subfamily beside the chip (subs, by the object's type: the bytes, a word's low byte, that hold it), BN5's is read as BN6's of BN6's chip (behaviour6: its record's, or the moved code's entry), where it is BN5's record's (+0x0C). The Navi chip's object, the fourth kind's 0x10, spawned by the Navi family's routine (BN5's family 0x41 at 0x080EC458, BN6's 0x1B at 0x080ED690, the same steps) through its spawner (BN5 0x080E1AC0, BN6 0x080E2C6C): the AttackVars' subfamily (+3) its +0x3C, the spawner's ldr r1,[r0,#0x3c]; strb r1,[r0,#0x19] (BN5 0x080E1AEC-0x080E1AEE) its +0x19 too, and the chip (+0x14, +6 above it) its +0x30; a Navi chip moved as BN5's Navi routine S runs as BN6's 0x1D + S (chip_numbrman: 0 as 0x1D, chip_shadoman 0xB as 0x28, at t33)

code_twins.why: A routine's address an object keeps (a Thumb pointer into each game's own code) is the same routine where both games' routines are twins: the same instructions but for the calls' targets, each game's own twin. Listed by pair, each pair's bodies compared (pairs). And a moved family's code may keep a routine of BN5's engine as a callback (its attack's variables +0x28, a jump table of its own): the install names BN6's twin there (the recipe's words). The snapshot reads such a word of BN5's as the twin the family's recipe gives it, where BN6's word is that twin: a translation by the recipe's pairs, each pair's bodies compared by tools/xrecipe.py (the same, the same but for the offsets of loads and stores, or a differing pair its audit takes, bn5_twins.AUDITS); a word aimed elsewhere in BN6 stays a difference.
evidence: tests/xdiff/families.json, code_twins: each family's pairs, written by tools/xrecipe.py with src/emu/xvirus_bn5.c

t3_type.why: An attack's type (+1), by its number in BN5 where BN5's is moved: BN6 spawns a moved type of the family's (CanGard's reticle, BN5's third kind's type 0x25) as the second-level dispatch's type of its kind (the first's 0x5C, the third's 0xD2, the fourth's 0x91: xvirus_recipe.h, XV_T*_DISPATCH), its BN5 number in the kind's side table by the object's slot (BN6_DISPATCH_SIDE: the first kind's at 0x0203FF00, the third's at 0x0203FF20, the fourth's at 0x0203FF40), and the dispatch runs it as that number. The trace writes the side table's byte beside each object of a dispatch type (src/dev/xdiff.c, version 3) and the snapshot reads its type as that byte (tools/xdiff_snap.py): a translation, not a mask, so a moved type keeps its BN5 number in both and is the same. The spawn hook reads the dispatch's spawner's frame the same way (its BN5 type and its caller, src/dev/xdiff_events.c). A twin of BN6's is spawned as BN6's own number, and mapped here where the numbers differ: BN5's lance (the misc family's subfamily 4, DrkLance's over its twin BN6's Lance) is its third kind's 0x4F, BN6's the same code at its 0x6F.
evidence: the dispatch's spawner (src/emu/xvirus_dispatch.c, the project's own Thumb): push {r0,lr}; TWIN by the type's low byte; XV_TYPE_MOVED spawns the kind's dispatch type; after BN6's spawner, the type into the side table at the object's slot (+3); its frame above BN6's spawner's five words: the type at +0x1C, its caller at +0x20
the dispatch type's routine: ldrb r0,[r5,#3]; the side table's byte; MOVED's routine for it, r1 the type times four as BN5's runner leaves it (BN5 0x08003014-0x0800301E / BN6 0x080031F4-0x080031FE)
BN6's runner reads +1 alone and its spawn writes it alone (BN6 0x080031F4, 0x080032BE); the moved code never reads it (the installer refuses ldrb rX,[r5,#1] in a moved block)

the lance: BN5's third kind's 0x4F (0x080CF938) and BN6's 0x6F (0x080D3CD0) the same instructions (tools/xrecipe_thumb.py's compare: SAME), spawned by each game's misc subfamily 4 (BN5 0x1A, BN6 0x1C, the registry's DrkLance twin 119); chip_drklance

effect.why: An effect object's id (+4 of the fourth kind's type 0): CanGard's muzzle blast is BN5's 0x57, copied as BN6's 0x6C (the immediate at BN5 0x08108FB6). The Navis' own effects take numbers from 0xA0, the Navis' range, one a BN5 effect whichever Navi (or the sea's marker, tools/bn5_objects.py) spawns it (src/emu/xnavi_bn5.c, its effects: tools/xnavirecipe.py), and an effect BN6 draws alike is BN6's (Colonel's 0x47, his strike's: BN6's 0x60, list 4's 0x0A the same bytes as BN5's list 4's 0x2C, its animation and palette 0, tools/xrecipe.py's effect_twin), read so only where a spec's foes hold one of its ids (navis): BN5's engine and its other enemies spawn those BN5 ids for effects of their own (the Mettaur's 0x14), each compared as BN6's of its number. BN5's sea's splash (0x63, a non-Aqua object stepping onto sea: BN5_PANEL_ARRIVED) is BN6's 0xAC wherever it is spawned, the moved objects' copy (tools/bn5_objects.py, ENGINE_EFFECTS; src/emu/xsea.c spawns it). The Souls' (the Souls track's S4, tools/xsoul.py) share the other tracks' copies: ColonelSoul's ScreenDivide's three, BN5's 0x48-0x4A (its family 0x43's base 0x48 + its sub-family, BN5 0x080EEE18), are the Navis' 0xA8-0xAA, TomahawkSoul's swing 0x45 the Navis' 0xA6, ShadowSoul's slash 0x17 (its sword family's sub-family 2, BN5's table 0x080EC112) the Navis' 0xA3: BN6 has an effect of the same record (0x17, and 0x33 for 0x45: its list, number, animation and palette) whose sprite, redrawn, animates for other frames, and an effect lives as long as its animation (copies).

copies.why: In a spec with the Souls installed (souls6), or whose spec asks (effect_copies: the obstacle strike's, colonel_strike): BN5's effects the Souls' code spawns that BN6's engine spawns of its own too (0x14 and 0x02, BN6's redrawn: 0x02 by a counter's family 0x47, BN6's twin of BN5's 0x2C), and ShadowSoul's slash 0x17 (BN6's of the same record redrawn, another animation), run as the Navis' copies of BN5's (one BN6 number a BN5 effect, issue #82's allocations: 0xA0, 0xA2, 0xA3, src/emu/xnavi_bn5.c), and the Souls' own copies, 0x03 (the unison's phase 0 spawns BN6's own) at 0xC0 and the obstacle strike's shot's hit 0x20 (its table 0x080C6C08, row 12, fixed in the chips' copy: tools/bn5_twins.py's SHARED_ROWS) at 0xC1, each drawn with BN5's sprite: a BN6 copy is read as the BN5 effect it copies, BN5's id as itself in both (which of the two a spawn is, the code that spawned it says). ColonelSoul's ScreenDivide's three (0x48-0x4A) and TomahawkSoul's swing (0x45) are the Navis' 0xA8-0xAA and 0xA6, read as such in every spec (tools/xdiff_snap.py's chip_effects, the chips' units naming them). The Navis' 0xAB, Colonel's copy of BN5's 0x01, the same: in colonel_strike BN6's engine spawns its own 0x01 where BN5's spawns 0x01, and Colonel's code the copy.

flash.why: A muzzle flash (the first kind's type 5, spawned by BN5 0x080B9CAE / BN6 0x080BA6A0 with its number in r4, kept at +4) is drawn by the entry of that number in each game's table of flashes, 5 bytes each (BN5 0x080B9A5C, BN6 0x080BA444, read at BN5 0x080B9BA8 / BN6 0x080BA570: its list, sprite, animation and palette): BN6 numbers the same flash otherwise. Each pair here names the same entry, or the same picture (the sprites byte for byte) at another number of list 3. The image object's own kinds, BN5's object moved once for every track (tools/bn5_objects.py: the Navis' images, the chips' muzzle flashes, the Souls' arm flashes and MegaMan's buster's in a Soul, src/emu/soullook.c), keep BN5's numbers in both games, the one copy run through the second-level dispatch: compared as they are (ob.moved).

panel_type.why: A panel's type (+2), the type it is drawn as (+6, the one-frame override's at +8) and the low nibble of its flags (BN5's +0x18, BN6's +0x14, the type ORed into its table's word): BN5's lava (8) and sea (0xA) are BN6's free types 13 and 14 where src/emu/xpanels.c brings them in, BN5's holy (9) BN6's 5 (src/emu/xfields.c), the rest the same numbers.
evidence: the flags: _object_updatePanelParameters ORs the type into its word, BN5 0x0800AFE0 / BN6 IWRAM 0x030078DC (ldrb r1,[r0,#2]; ... orrs r1,r3)

the drawn type: the same routines copy +2 to +6; BN5's per-panel update writes lava's 8 or 2 there as it blinks (0x0800AA68), BN6's its conveyors' own type or 2 (0x0800C478), the path lava and sea take in BN6 (xpanels.c, panel_ages)
the flags' words: lava's 0x11010 and the sea's 0x30010 are BN5's (BN5_PANEL_FLAGS_OF), copied into BN6's grown table (xpanels.c, flags_make)

alliance.why: A collision data's +0x30 (what it is) and +0x34 (what it strikes) are words the engine's setup takes from a table by the object's alliance and a region its caller names, two words a region, and ORs the time stop's bit 0x10000 into +0x30 while time is stopped; each game has its own table (layouts, collision, alliance_masks), whose entries mostly differ by BN6's bit 0x80. So a BN5 word is read as the BN6 entry at its place in BN5's table (with the time stop's bit as it is): over the 160 entries each BN5 word gives one BN6 word (a word two entries would give otherwise would be left as it is; none does). A hit and a touch OR the other object's +0x30 into what hit or touched it (BN6's +0x70 and +0x6C, BN5's +0x68 and +0x64): such a word is read as the OR of the BN6 words of the table's words it is made of, where every way of making it gives the same (else it is compared as it is), its bit 0x01 as it is: the hit pass's own where an attack struck a guard, no table word's. Not the family's code: the setup and the hit pass are the engine's, and the family's region and alliance are compared through them (a family object set up with another region reads as another BN6 word). A BN5 word two places give otherwise, BN6's with bit 0x80 at one and without at the other (BN5's 0 is BN6's 0 at region 0 and 0x80 at others), is read as BN6's where BN6's is either: the place is the setup's own (its r1 and r2), which no trace records.
evidence: the setup: BN5 0x08016760-0x080167AE / BN6 0x08019FB4-0x0801A00C, the same steps: +0x30 from the table's reader (BN5 0x08016BBC / BN6 0x0801A0BA: alliance x 4 + region x 8) for the region in r1, stored at BN5 0x0801678A / BN6 0x08019FE8; 0x10000 ORed in where the time stop's test (BN5 0x08008A78 / BN6 0x0800A098, bit 2 of the battle's flags) is set (BN5 0x08016792-0x0801679C / BN6 0x08019FF0-0x08019FFA); +0x34 for the region in r2 (BN5 0x080167A6 / BN6 0x0801A004)

the tables (layouts, collision, alliance_masks): BN5 0x08016364 reads 0x08410000, 0x04210000, 0x80000000, 0x40000000 (entries 2, 3, 8, 9) where BN6 0x08019C7C reads 0x08410080, 0x04210080, 0x80000080, 0x40000080; entries 4-7, 10, 11 alike in both; of BN5's 160 words 128 have their BN6 entry with the bit, 30 the same word, region 61's two (BN5 0x80000080, 0x40000080) BN6's 0x80

the hit pass ORs the hitter's +0x30 into what hit it: BN5 0x080169E8-0x080169F2, 0x08016A28-0x08016A34 (its +0x6C/+0x70, then +0x68) / BN6 0x081D7800-0x081D7804, 0x081D783A-0x081D7840 (+0x70); the second pass into what touched it: BN5 0x080174AA-0x080174B0 (+0x64) / BN6 0x081D7BD2-0x081D7BD8 (+0x6C)
BN6's use of its bit: its second pass lets an object whose +0x3C has 0x20 touch only one whose +0x30 has 0x80 (0x081D7BAE-0x081D7BD0); BN5's twin 0x0801748C has no such test

in the traces of every spec each +0x30 and +0x34, and each hit and touch word on the frames compared, reads as its BN6 word: MegaMan's 0x08410000, CanGard's and the Mettaur's 0x04210000, the reticle's 0x40000000, MegaMan's shots' 0x80000000, each with 0x80 in BN6; a reticle's hit word 0x08410000 (MegaMan's) as 0x08410080

the guard's bit: where the struck object's +0x3C has bit 0x01 (guarding: KnightMan's) and the attack's +0x30 has neither of 0x1002, the hit pass ORs 1 into what hit the attack: BN5 0x080169B0-0x080169CA (its +0x6C + 4 x the struck's side) / BN6 0x081D77C4-0x081D77E2 (+0x70); none of the 160 words of either table has bit 0x01 (their low bits are 0x02-0xA0); knightman_v1_keys' buster shot at t39 on KnightMan guarding: BN5's 0x04210001, BN6's 0x04210081

renderer.why: Each frame the sprite renderer hands each object it draws a place for its tiles in OBJ VRAM (its sprite state's +0x08, u16) from a running count over all it draws before it, and a palette slot (+0x15's high nibble) from the slots taken before it; a frame or palette already loaded this frame is given its place or slot again. The code is the same in both games, but what each draws (MegaMan's own sprite, his flash and sparks, BN6's own effects, a native) differs, so the numbers do. A family object's place and slot are read as their rank among those the family's objects drawn that frame take: the family's own draw order and sharing, compared; what else is drawn among them is no part of the family's. One not drawn (its +0x00 bit 0x02 clear, its sprite's state's +0x03 bit 0x02 clear: the renderer's own test, as an object can hide its sprite alone; or its cache, +0x24, clear: the renderer passed it over, NumberMan's companion while visible) keeps the place it was last drawn at, so it keeps that rank; one whose place moved undrawn is compared as it is; one never drawn has no place the renderer gave it (its sprite state holds its slot's last occupant's, or its set-up's; its spawn clears its record short of them): none, in both. Slot 15 (none taken) stays. The frames the family draws are compared from its sprite's own data (+0x1C, +0x20) and its cache (+0x24), so its tile counts are. The same places of what is not the family's are masked (the renderer's slots, the renderer's palette slot). A family object whose place (or slot) in BN5 is one an object not the family's draws that frame (the renderer keeps a frame or palette already loaded where it is: the Dark Soul's buster's arm and muzzle, 3:0x03 and 3:0x06, the same art as BN5's MegaMan's own, which BN6's MegaMan draws from BN6's) is ranked in neither game, read as shared in both (tools/xdiff_masks.py, SHARED).
evidence: the renderer: BN5 0x081C7F26-0x081C804C and BN6 0x081D64BE-0x081D65E4 (the IWRAM renderer's ROM copies), the same code but for their literal pools

a sprite's state not shown is skipped, its cache cleared and its place kept: BN5 0x081C7F9A-0x081C7FAC / BN6 0x081D6532-0x081D6544 (ldrb [r5,#3]; tst #2); metfire_v1: the fire column's object shown and its sprite not (t199-t203, t317-t321), its place the one it was last given (BN5 29, BN6 59), and a column's place before its first draw its slot's last occupant's (t247: BN5 59, BN6 29)

the tile place: BN5 0x081C7FF4-0x081C7FFC / BN6 0x081D658C-0x081D6594, the running count's value stored and the frame's tiles added to it (BN6 0x081D6562-0x081D6566, 0x081D6590-0x081D6594); a frame already copied this frame is given its place again (found at BN6 0x081D66A8-0x081D66C6, stored at 0x081D65B8); a sprite not drawn keeps its old place, its cache cleared (BN6 0x081D653A-0x081D6544)
